newsitem.title: USA: FEATURE - U.S. insurers could be a casualty in tobacco wars.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE - U.S. insurers could be a casualty in tobacco wars.

text.p: The U.S. insurance industry is growing increasingly worried that it could be among the casualties if tobacco companies begin to suffer costly losses in their legal battles.
"I think it's like an inching toward the realisation that there's some potential (for losses)," an industry source said.
Part of the reason is that tobacco settlement negotiations and smoking-related lawsuits may help push the insurance industry's day of reckoning a little closer, he said.
"That would quicken the pace that the insurance industry would have to respond to this kind of issue," he said.
Most in the industry still believe the chances of a major insured loss is slim, but the stakes are so high and the future so unpredictable that the threat is hard to ignore.
